1 لَهِثَ , aor.
لَهَثَ , inf. n. لَهَثٌ and لَهَاثٌ and لَهَثَانٌ, He thirsted; was thirsty: (S, K:) or thirst heated his belly, or inside. (L.) ―
-b2- لَهَثَ, aor.
لَهَثَ , inf. n. لَهْثٌ and لُهَاثٌ; (S, K;) and لَهِثَ, aor.
لَهَثَ ; (TA;) and ↓ التهث ; (K;) He (a dog, S, and a man, and, in the case of the second verb, a bird also, TA) put forth his tongue, by reason of thirst, or fatigue, or weariness: (S, K:) or لَهَثَ signifies his breath (نفس) rose, by reason of fatigue, or weariness: or he (a dog) put forth his tongue, by reason of thirst: and he (a man) was fatigued, or weary. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
